title: Welcome to the Dungeon Dive!
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Aq3emUbqTbA

Daniel (@dungeondive) introduces the channel in forty seconds flat. This is the Dungeon Dive's founding document, and it is almost comically direct: if you like killing monsters and taking their stuff, rolling handfuls of dice, finding lots of loot and treasure, and having random encounters in and out of dungeons, this is the channel for you.

That is the entire pitch. There is no roadmap, no upload schedule, no subscriber goal. Daniel names the remit — all kinds of dungeon crawls and fantasy adventure games, and games tangentially related to those two — hopes you like what you see, and signs off.

What earns it a place in the archive is how well the promise has held. The word "tangentially" turns out to be doing an enormous amount of work: it is the licence under which the channel would later cover solo RPGs, vintage paperbacks, video games, dungeon synth records and a chili recipe, without ever once feeling like it had wandered off. Everything the Dungeon Dive became is either named here outright or quietly admitted by that single adjective.

Worth watching as a time capsule from April 2018, when the whole enterprise was one person, one hobby room, and forty seconds of stated intent.

----

Channel trailers usually age badly. Does this one hold up because the promise was broad enough to absorb anything, or because Daniel simply kept it?
